title: Systems and Center of Mass
short: Choose what is in your system; its center of mass is the mass-weighted average position.
trouble: Students put the center of mass halfway between two objects whatever their masses.

blocks.html: Newton's Second Law: F = ma relates the net force on an object to its acceleration. But what counts as "the object"? A car with passengers, two carts tied together, a whole train? In physics you get to choose: the things you include form the system, and everything else is the surroundings.

Forces between parts of the system are internal; forces from outside are external. Only external forces change the motion of the system's center of mass, the mass-weighted average position: $x_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1x_1 + m_2x_2 + \cdots}{m_1 + m_2 + \cdots}$.

Internal forces come in third-law pairs, equal and opposite, both inside the system, so they cancel when you add up all the forces on the system. What's left is the external force, and it moves the system as if all the mass sat at one point. That point is a weighted mean: like a fair share, but heavier parts get more say.

blocks.name: ph-torque

opts.task: The pivot sits under the center of mass, so the seesaw balances. Where would the pivot need to go if the masses were equal?

blocks.cap: A 30 kg child at 0.5 m and a 20 kg child at 3.0 m: $x_{cm} = \dfrac{15 + 60}{50} = 1.5\ \text{m}$, closer to the heavier child.

blocks.title: Two masses
blocks.q: A $6\ \text{kg}$ block sits at $x = 0$ and a $2\ \text{kg}$ block at $x = 4\ \text{m}$. Where is their center of mass?
steps: $x_{cm} = 1\ \text{m}$: a quarter of the way, close to the heavier block, not halfway.

blocks.title: Three masses
blocks.q: Masses of $2$, $3$ and $5\ \text{kg}$ sit at $x = 0$, $1$ and $3\ \text{m}$. Find $x_{cm}$.

blocks.title: Choosing the system
blocks.q: A tow truck pulls a car with a chain. Which forces are internal if the system is the truck, the chain and the car?
steps: Internal: the chain's pull on the car and the car's pull back on the chain; the truck's pull on the chain and the chain's pull back. Each pair cancels within the system.
External: gravity, the road's normal and friction forces on the tires, air drag. Only these change the motion of the whole rig.
blocks.a: The chain forces are internal; road, gravity and air forces are external.

blocks.html: Putting the center of mass halfway between two objects whatever their masses. Halfway is right only for equal masses. Check: the center of mass is always between the objects and closer to the heavier one; if one mass is much bigger, it sits almost on top of that mass.
